reply_text:
*I’d hold the merge.* Reviewed `feature-flags-rules` at `e3396ff` against `main`; two rollout-safety issues:

1. *High — Rules leak between independent flags* — `flags/registry.py:13–15`
   `rules=[]` is shared across calls. Creating a staff-only flag, then a separate free-plan flag, makes the staff-only flag enable for free-plan customers too: both flags reference the same list, and `Flag.enabled()` accepts any matching rule (`:9–10`).
   *Recommended fix:* use a `None` default and construct a fresh rules list per call. Add a regression test creating two different flags without explicitly passing `[]`. Current registry tests always pass a list, hiding this bug.

2. *High — Missing fields can now satisfy string rules* — `flags/match.py:2`
   Stringifying everything converts a missing field into `"none"`. Verified: `matches({'region': 'none'}, {})` now returns `True`, whereas it returned `False` on `main`. Explicit null also matches the literal string `"none"`, potentially expanding rollout eligibility unexpectedly.
   *Recommended fix:* distinguish missing/null values before normalization; restrict coercion to the intended string/integer cases. Add missing-field and null-versus-string regression tests.

All five existing tests pass; I reproduced both issues with separate in-memory checks. No files changed.
